back: An uncertain event or condition that, if it occurs, has a positive or negative effect on objectives.
Threat: negative effect (delay, overrun, reputation). Opportunity: positive effect (savings, market share).
Cause, event and consequence: separates the risk from its causes and effects.
The effect of uncertainty on the project as a whole; if too high, the project may be cancelled.
The degree of uncertainty an organization or person will accept in anticipation of a reward.
Measurable acceptable variation around an objective; ±5% shows a lower appetite than ±10%.
The aggregate potential impact of all risks at a point in time.
Known-known (not a risk), known-unknown (classic risk), unknown-known (hidden fact), unknown-unknown (emergent risk).
The ability to absorb impacts and recover quickly, including from black swans and emergent risks.
Begins when the project is conceived; completed early.
Strategy, methodology, roles, funding, timing, risk categories, stakeholder risk appetite, probability and impact definitions.
A hierarchy of potential risk sources, e.g. technical, management, commercial, external.
Project-specific; typically five levels for a detailed process, three for a simple one.
Brainstorming, checklists, interviews, root cause, assumption and constraint, SWOT, document analysis, prompt lists, meetings, AI.
Predetermined risk categories: lowest RBS level for individual risks; PESTLE, TECOP, VUCA for overall risk.
Opportunities from strengths, threats from weaknesses; adds internally generated risks.
Finds threats in assumptions that are inaccurate, unstable, inconsistent or incomplete.
Identified risks (ID, statement), potential owners and responses; category, status, causes, effects, triggers, timing.
An event or condition indicating that a risk is about to occur.
Sources of overall project risk plus summary data on individual risks (counts, categories, trends).
Probability and impact for every risk, throughout; also urgency, manageability, relationships; uses the P-I matrix.
Low-probability, low-impact risks kept in the register for monitoring.
Numerical analysis of combined effects on overall objectives; not always required; simulation, sensitivity, decision trees.
Shows sensitivity analysis: risks ordered by how strongly they affect the outcome.
Probability × impact in money; threats negative, opportunities positive; used in decision trees.
